=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py: line 157 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: `template_command_inventory` reads `workflow-templates/.claude/commands` from the PR checkout, not a protected-base support checkout.
  WHY: A PR that includes a new template twin gets its matching command path into the frozen admitted set.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh: line 2162 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: `admitted_inventory_missing` is absent from the transfer-reason allowlist.
  WHY: A transfer rejected due to missing or corrupt admitted-command inventory reports `reason=unknown` instead of the specific reason.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Fix the admissible command names at snapshot time from a protected-base template inventory; reuse that immutable set for every transfer and reject newly admitted paths."
  Expected change site: scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py, snapshot() and template_command_inventory()
  Evidence of absence: The inventory IS frozen at snapshot time and transfer/refresh reuse the immutable set — those parts are satisfied. The "protected-base" qualifier is not satisfied: template_command_inventory() at line 66-78 reads workflow-templates/.claude/commands from the host checkout, which is the PR head (review_untrusted_sandbox.sh:37). The PR controls which template twins exist at snapshot time, so the inventory is not sourced from a PR-immutable support tree. The described TOCTOU retry race IS fixed; the protected-base gap is a defense-in-depth shortfall against a PR that adds its own template twin.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh: 2162 (case statement) vs scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:274 (new reason_code entry) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The new `admitted_inventory_missing` reason code is not in the bash case-statement allowlist.
  WHY: The diagnostic falls through to `transfer_reason=unknown`, masking the specific fail-closed reason.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py: 35 (allowed), 111 (enumerate_workspace) — `host` parameter signature | severity=NIT | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The `host` parameter is dead code on all reachable post-snapshot paths.
  WHY: It invites future callers to pass a host they expect to be consulted, potentially re-opening the inventory-source vulnerability.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Fix the admissible command names at snapshot time from a protected-base template inventory; reuse that immutable set for every transfer and reject newly admitted paths."
  Expected change site: scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py::template_command_inventory (and its call site in snapshot, line 157)
  Evidence of absence: The fix snapshots whatever files exist at host/workflow-templates/.claude/commands/ at the moment of the snapshot call. The `host` argument is `${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}` (scripts/review_untrusted_sandbox.sh:8, 37), and review_autofix.yml:2531 checks out `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` — the PR head. The PR head is precisely the surface the editor can write to before the snapshot, so the inventory is still sourced from PR-controlled content. A PR that adds a new template twin `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/<name>.md` before the snapshot will be admitted into the frozen inventory, and the editor can then write `.claude/commands/<name>.md` on any subsequent transfer. The test at test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py:8181-8283 does not exercise this scenario: it creates the template inside the same `host` directory the script inventories, so it only proves the inventory is frozen AFTER snapshot, not that its source is protected. A "protected base" path (e.g. the base branch's workflow-templates/.claude/commands/ resolved independently of the PR head, as the workflow already does for .codex-workflow-src) is absent.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh: line 2162 | PROBLEM: The transfer diagnostic allowlist omits the new admitted_inventory_missing reason code.
  WHY: The workflow falls back to `transfer_reason=unknown`, degrading diagnostic specificity; the transfer is still rejected.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Fix the admissible command names at snapshot time from a protected-base template inventory; reuse that immutable set for every transfer and reject newly admitted paths."
  Expected change site: `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py`, `template_command_inventory()` and `snapshot()`.
  Evidence of absence: The implementation freezes the inventory at snapshot time (line 157: `commands = template_command_inventory(host)`, line 178: writes the frozen set to `admitted_commands_path(manifest)`), and `transfer`/`refresh` load it via `load_admitted_commands(manifest)` (lines 189, 232). This correctly prevents the editor from widening admission during a run — the exploit described in the issue. However, `template_command_inventory(host)` reads `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/` from the PR-head checkout (`review_autofix.yml:2531` checks out `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`), not from a protected base (main/stable). A PR author who adds a template twin in the PR diff gets the matching `.claude/commands/<name>.md` admitted at snapshot time, which the editor could then create. This is a different threat model than the issue's exploit (editor mutating the host during a transfer), and the agents.md update (lines 72-82) explicitly documents the intended behavior as "fixed for the whole run." The "protected-base" language in the recommendation is reasonably interpreted as "frozen/immutable at snapshot time" rather than "sourced from main/stable," since sourcing from main/stable would break legitimate PR additions of new commands. The fix satisfies the described exploit scenario.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2
